title: A small PHP app for teaching the web

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do you teach students a whole web stack without drowning them in a framework? Antoine's answer is TCH099, a small PHP demo app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It serves a few pages and a JSON API for sign-up, login, logout and user details, plus an admin page that lists the accounts. An Android app talks to the same API.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: None. Two files handle the routing, a handful of scripts do the work, and one table in MariaDB holds the accounts. Because it's so small, you can read all of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Docker locally, with Apache. On Azure App Service it goes behind nginx, and a GitHub Actions workflow deploys it when you push to main.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is the code the only teaching material?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. There's a documentation site in French for teams starting a project: user stories, the API reference, a tour of the browser DevTools, the Android setup and the Azure deployment steps, with sequence diagrams for each call.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A full learning path built on a tiny app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The written page has the diagrams.
